decisions.rationale: Lead Metagross+Incineroar applies immediate offensive pressure with FakeOut protection and Meteor Mash. Incin's Intimidate weakens physical threats (Archaludon, Scizor, Staraptor). Torkoal (back 1) sets Sun to override opponent's Rain and power Eruption/Heat Wave. Mamoswine (back 2) provides Ice Shard priority for Noivern/Staraptor and High Horsepower for Archaludon. Intended Mega: Metagross. This lead handles Grimmsnarl/Politoed disruption while keeping TR+Sun options flexible for mid-game.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs Rain (Politoed/Drizzle) + fast Tailwind (Noivern) modes. Prankster Grimmsnarl is key support threat—Hatterene's Magic Bounce hard counters it. Archaludon is Life Orb Modest, dangerous in Rain with ElectroShot. Scizor holds Mega Stone; evaluate as base forme until Mega'd. Staraptor has Expert Belt BraveBird/CloseCombat. My Sun+TR dual speed control can override their speed advantages. Incineroar FakeOut + Intimidate is critical turn-1 tool against their physical attackers. Mamoswine Ice Shard priority handles fast Flying/Dragon threats. Plan: Lead aggressive, pivot to Sun or TR depending on opponent's speed control choice.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Scizor. Lead Politoed+Archaludon: Drizzle rain neuters Fire and enables Electro Shot +1 SpA boost; Archaludon resists Metagross Steel (0.5x) and 2HKOs with Electro Shot (42-96%). Back: Noivern Tailwind+rain Hurricane OHKOs Meowscarada; Scizor-Mega walls Metagross, BP 2HKOs Hatterene, CC hits Mamoswine. If Torkoal sun overrides, switch Politoed out and back in.
decisions.notebook:
Durable facts for series:
- Torkoal (Quiet, 36-64 Spe) slower than Politoed (Calm, 90 Spe): Drought overrides Drizzle if both lead. Must switch Politoed out/back to re-set rain.
- Archaludon Electro Shot is NEUTRAL on Metagross (Electric vs Steel = neutral, NOT NVE). 42-96% from 194 SpA+LO. With rain +1 SpA, potential OHKO. Earthquake vs Metagross: 22-48% (SE but physical 112 Atk, spread-reduced) — weak.
- Archaludon resists Metagross Meteor Mash/Bullet Punch at 0.5x (NOT quad-resist; Steel vs Steel 0.5x × Dragon 1x). Ice Punch neutral. Stamina boosts Def each hit.
- Politoed Weather Ball in rain = Water 100 BP (weather doubles), ×1.5 rain ×1.5 STAB = 225 BP. Neutral on Metagross (Water vs Steel = neutral, NOT SE). 33-72%.
- Scizor-Mega Close Combat vs Metagross = NEUTRAL (Fighting vs Steel SE × Psychic NVE = 1x). Bullet Punch vs Hatterene = SE (Steel vs Fairy 2x), 2HKO. Close Combat vs Mamoswine = SE (Fighting vs Ice 2x). U-turn vs Hatterene = neutral (Bug vs Psychic SE × Fairy NVE).
- Noivern Hurricane vs Meowscarada = SE (Flying vs Grass 2x). Rain Hurricane = 100% acc. Noivern 192 Spe speed-ties Meowscarada (157-192).
- Water is neutral on Steel (not SE). Electric is neutral on Steel (not NVE). Fighting is neutral on Steel/Psychic (SE×NVE).
- Opponent Mega: Metagross-Mega (Tough Claws, 143-178 Spe). Only Mega Stone on their team.
- Plan: Rain core Politoed+Archaludon+Noivern + Mega Scizor. Override Torkoal sun by switching Politoed. Noivern for Tailwind+Meowscarada. Scizor-Mega for Metagross wall+Hatterene/Mamoswine cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Protect Metagross to avoid Archaludon's super-effective Earthquake (25.7-46.7%) or potential ElectroShot. Incineroar Fake Outs Politoed to disrupt their rain support—either flinching them or forcing a wasted Protect. This is a safe, information-gathering turn 1 that preserves both my Pokémon while testing opponent's intentions. Neither of my attacks OHKO Politoed, so aggressive plays are risky.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs Rain mode with Politoed/Drizzle. Archaludon is Life Orb Modest with dangerous ElectroShot in rain. Prankster Grimmsnarl is key support threat. Scizor holds Mega Stone. My Sun+TR dual speed control can override their speed advantages. Incineroar FakeOut + Intimidate is critical turn-1 tool. Plan: Lead aggressive, pivot to Sun or TR depending on opponent's speed control choice. Hatterene's Magic Bounce hard counters Prankster support.

decisions.rationale: Protect (+4) guaranteed beats Fake Out (+3) on Archaludon. Weather Ball (67-121%) breaks Incineroar's Focus Sash, leaving it at 1 HP. Next turn Fake Out is spent, Archaludon freely Electro Shots Metagross with rain still active. Even if opponent redirects Fake Out to Politoed, Archaludon stays full HP and both attack freely next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 T1: Led Archaludon+Politoed vs Metagross+Incineroar. Rain up from Drizzle. Opponent Incineroar has Focus Sash. Electro Shot on Metagross without +1 SpA: 36-66%; with +1 SpA from rain: ~55-99% (not guaranteed OHKO). Weather Ball on Incineroar: 68-121% (Sash saves at 1HP). Protect priority +4 beats Fake Out +3. Plan: T2 Archaludon Electro Shot Metagross (rain still up, no Fake Out threat), Politoed picks off 1HP Incineroar or Helping Hand. Watch for Metagross-Mega 143-178 Spe outspeeding everything. Opponent back 4 unknown: Torkoal, Mamoswine, Meowscarada, Hatterene likely.

decisions.rationale: Mega Metagross targets Politoed with Tough Claws-boosted Meteor Mash to remove rain setter. Incineroar Protects to avoid 2x Weather Ball in rain and potential Archaludon Earthquake. If Metagross outspeeds Archaludon (134 vs 105-137), we KO or heavily damage Politoed before it acts. If Archaludon is faster, Incin's Protect blocks EQ while Metagross still threatens Politoed. Removing Politoed ends rain, crippling Archaludon's ElectroShot and enabling our Sun/TR win conditions.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs Rain with Politoed/Drizzle + Archaludon Life Orb. Archaludon is Modest special attacker; -1 Atk from Intimidate irrelevant. Prankster Grimmsnarl on bench is key support threat. Scizor holds Mega Stone. My Sun+TR modes can override their speed. Incin FakeOut+Intimidate critical turn-1 tool. Always prioritize removing Politoed to end rain. Mega Metagross Tough Claws provides necessary damage boost against NVE Steel targets. Watch for Grimmsnarl screens enabling sweepers.

decisions.rationale: Opponent cannot KO either of my Pokémon this turn—Meteor Mash 14-24%, Ice Punch 16-27%, Flare Blitz 0.25x in rain. Electro Shot does 47-85% to Metagross and grants +1 SpA; next turn +1 SpA Electro Shot reaches 71-128% (likely KO). Weather Ball does 68-121% to Incineroar, breaking Focus Sash. Next turn Politoed easily picks off 1 HP Incineroed while Archaludon KOs Metagross. Spreading damage is more consistent than gambling on a Helping Hand KO.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 T2 plan: Archaludon Electro Shot on Metagross (47-85%, +1 SpA from rain charge), Politoed Weather Ball on Incineroar (68-121%, breaks Sash). Opponent damage output negligible in rain: Mega Metagross Meteor Mash 14-24% on Archaludon, Ice Punch 16-27% (neutral, not NVE as I initially thought—Steel resists Ice but Dragon is weak, netting 1x). Flare Blitz 0.25x in rain on Water/Steel. Next turn: +1 SpA Electro Shot should KO Metagross (71-128%), Politoed picks off 1 HP Incineroar. Watch for Metagross-Mega 143-178 Spe outspeeding everything. Opponent back 4: Torkoal (Drought threat to rain), Mamoswine (Ice Shard SE on Archaludon/Noivern), Meowscarada (157-192 Spe, Protean), Hatterene (TR, Magic Bounce). Scizor-Mega and Noivern on bench for speed control and late-game. Key win con: Archaludon +1 SpA sweep in rain with Electro Shot.

decisions.rationale: Metagross at 9% HP must Protect—Electro Shot (25-44%) or Earthquake (2x) will KO otherwise. Incineroar Flare Blitz into Politoed (18-34% NVE) chips the rain setter; removing Drizzle is the win condition. Both targets resist Fire, but Politoed is the priority to end rain support for Archaludon.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's core is Rain (Politoed/Drizzle) + Archaludon Life Orb special attacker. Archaludon Modest with +1 SpA is dangerous but -1 Atk from Intimidate is irrelevant. Prankster Grimmsnarl on bench provides screens support. Scizor holds Mega Stone. My Sun+TR modes can override their speed control. Always prioritize removing Politoed to end rain. Mega Metagross Tough Claws is essential for damage vs NVE Steel targets. Watch for Grimmsnarl Reflect/LightScreen enabling sweepers. Incin FakeOut+Intimidate is critical turn-1 tool. Metagross-Mega is fragile when low HP—Protect is often mandatory.

decisions.rationale: Electro Shot guarantees KO on 8% Metagross. Weather Ball (100 BP STAB Water in rain, 2x SE) deals 61-132% to Incineroar, breaking Focus Sash or OHKOing. No friendly fire, both targets addressed. Even if Incineroar Parting Shots out, it eats the hit first and we go up 5-4 with Metagross eliminated and Archaludon +1 SpA intact for the sweep.
decisions.notebook: Opponent lead: Mega Metagross + Incineroar (Focus Sash, Intimidate). Back: Torkoal (Drought, Charcoal, Quiet 36-64 Spe), Mamoswine (Thick Fat, Life Orb, Adamant 100-132 Spe, Ice Shard), Meowscarada (Protean, Expert Belt, Jolly 157-192 Spe), Hatterene (Magic Bounce, Leftovers, Quiet 44-72 Spe, TR). Key threats: Torkoal sun overrides rain and enables Eruption; Mamoswine Ice Shard KOs Archaludon/Noivern; Meowscarada outspeeds everything; Hatterene TR reverses speed tiers and Magic Bounce blocks status. Win con: Archaludon +1 SpA Electro Shot sweep in rain. Scizor-Mega and Noivern on bench for speed control and late-game. Watch for Parting Shot pivots into Torkoal to flip weather.

decisions.rationale: Both Pokémon are at critical HP (9%/13%). Switching Metagross to Torkoal immediately overrides Rain with Drought Sun, removing Politoed's Weather Ball boost and Archaludon's Electro Shot charge. Incineroar Protects to survive the turn despite 50% success rate—safer than Parting Shot since Archaludon (faster) could Earthquake KO before Parting Shot executes. Torkoal's Sun enables Eruption next turn and neutralizes rain core.
decisions.notebook: Rain core (Politoed+Archaludon LO) is vulnerable to Sun override via Drought. Archaludon Modest +2 SpA is primary threat but -1 Atk from Intimidate persists. Prankster Grimmsnarl screens enable sweepers—watch for Reflect/LightScreen turns. Scizorite holder can Mega for priority BulletPunch sweeps. Preserve Incineroar for Intimidate/FakeOut utility; Mega Metagross Tough Claws essential vs NVE Steel. Switch low-HP Pokémon into Sun setter when rain is active rather than gambling Protects.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake guaranteed KOs both foes at 8% and 13% even at -1 Atk with spread reduction. Politoed Protects to avoid friendly fire. This play is immune to the Parting Shot→Torkoal→sun weather flip that would ruin Weather Ball targeting. If Incineroar outspeeds and Parting Shots, Earthquake still KOs Metagross and hits the switch-in (SE on Torkoal). Only risk is Metagross Protect at reduced rate, leaving it at 8% for an easy cleanup next turn.

Back: Torkoal (Drought, Charcoal, Quiet 36-64 Spe), Mamoswine (Thick Fat, Life Orb, Adamant 100-132 Spe, Ice Shard), Meowscarada (Protean, Expert Belt, Jolly 157-192 Spe), Hatterene (Magic Bounce, Leftovers, Quiet 44-72 Spe, TR). Win con: Archaludon +2 SpA sweep in rain. Scizor-Mega and Noivern on bench for speed control and late-game. Watch for Parting Shot pivots into Torkoal to flip weather. decisions.rationale: Archaludon +2 SpA LO is the primary threat; Torkoal at 75% likely dies to Electro Shot. Switching Metagross in via Incineroar is safest - Metagross resists Flash Cannon, is neutral to Electro Shot, and outspeeds Archaludon. Torkoal Protects to avoid double-target damage and preserve Sun setter. This preserves both key Pokémon while bringing in our win condition safely.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs Rain core (Politoed+Archaludon LO) vulnerable to Sun override. Archaludon Modest +2 SpA is primary threat but Intimidate -1 Atk persists. Prankster Grimmsnarl screens enable sweepers—watch for Reflect/LightScreen turns. Scizorite holder can Mega for priority BulletPunch sweeps. Preserve Incineroar for Intimidate/FakeOut utility; Mega Metagross Tough Claws essential vs NVE Steel. Switch low-HP Pokémon into Sun setter when rain is active rather than gambling Protects. Politoed Sitrus already consumed. Opponent showed tendency to Protect on turn after taking heavy damage.

decisions.rationale: Electro Shot at +2 SpA outspeeds and heavily damages/KOs Torkoal (40-95%), neutralizing the Eruption threat before it fires. Switching Politoed to Noivern brings in a 192-Speed Flying-type immune to Ground, with Focus Sash for safety. Even if Torkoal survives at low HP, its Eruption is negligible and Noivern outspeeds to finish it next turn. Incineroar at 13% is non-threatening — Parting Shot just pivots it out, Flare Blitz KOs itself via recoil.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Metagross-Mega (8%, Jolly, Metagrossite), Incineroar (Focus Sash broken, Impish, Intimidate, Parting Shot pivot), Torkoal (Drought/Charcoal/Quiet, Eruption spread threat in sun), Mamoswine (Thick Fat/Life Orb/Adamant, Ice Shard priority threatens Archaludon/Noivern), Meowscarada (Protean/Expert Belt/Jolly, fastest foe 157-192), Hatterene (Magic Bounce/Leftovers/Quiet, TR reverses speed). Win con: Archaludon +2 SpA sweep. Politoed Drizzle can re-set rain to override sun on re-entry. Noivern 192 Spe for speed control; Scizor-Mega for priority Bullet Punch and Mamoswine check. Watch Parting Shot into Mamoswine for Ice Shard KO on Archaludon. Sun has 4 turns left from Torkoal Drought; persists even if Torkoal KOed.

decisions.rationale: Metagross at 9% is extremely vulnerable to Noivern's Hurricane or Super Fang. Protecting guarantees survival while Torkoal pressures the +3 SpA Archaludon with SE Earth Power (41-97%). Even if Archaludon Protects, we preserve our Mega for future turns. Torkoal can tank one Earthquake (24-43%) at 75% HP.
decisions.notebook: Archaludon Modest +3 SpA with LO is primary win condition threat; must be pressured or KO'd. Noivern Timid Focus Sash can outspeed Mega Metagross. Opponent Protects after taking heavy damage. Politoed Sitrus consumed, brn'd. Preserve Mega Metagross for late-game; it's essential vs NVE Steel targets with Tough Claws. Incineroar at 13% with Focus Sash can still provide one Intimidate/Fake Out. Torkoal's Protect success rate degrades with consecutive use—avoid relying on it. Sun vs Rain weather war is key; Torkoal's Drought overrides Drizzle on switch-in.

decisions.rationale: Torkoal fainted; must switch. Mamoswine at 100% with LO HighHorsepower has the best chance to KO 71% Archaludon before +3 SpA LO Electro Shot sweeps. Incineroar at 13% loses Focus Sash protection and likely falls to Electro Shot immediately. Mega Metagross at 9% is too frail to survive spread Earthquake or any strong hit; its Steel moves are NVE vs both Steel-types. Mamoswine gives the only realistic path to remove the +3 SpA Archaludon threat.
decisions.notebook: Archaludon Modest LO +3 SpA is the primary win condition threat; must be KO'd before it fires another Electro Shot. Sun vs Rain weather war favors switching Torkoal back in later to override Drizzle. Incineroar Focus Sash intact but only triggers at full HP—preserve for late-game Intimidate or Fake Out support. Mega Metagross essential vs NVE Steel targets with Tough Claws but extremely vulnerable at low HP; avoid switching it into Earthquake spread. Opponent Protects after taking heavy damage—predict accordingly. Noivern Timid Focus Sash can outspeed Mega Metagross; keep Mamoswine Ice Shard ready for priority cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Electro Shot fires from turn-5 charge at +3 SpA, guaranteed KO on Torkoal (105 Spe > 36-64). Switching Noivern to Scizor preserves Focus Sash and brings in a complete Metagross wall (all moves 0.5x NVE on Bug/Steel). Scizor-Mega also counters opponent back: Bullet Punch 2x SE on Mamoswine/Hatterene, Close Combat 2x SE on Meowscarada/Incineroar. Next turn priority BP cleans up Metagross at 8%. Zero risk, strong endgame.
decisions.notebook: Electro Shot is 2-turn in sun (charges turn 1, fires turn 2; rain makes it 1-turn via Drizzle/Rain Dance). Hurricane accuracy 50% in sun, 100% in rain. Archaludon +3 SpA from 3 Electro Shot charges. Scizor-Mega walls Metagross-Mega (all moves 0.5x NVE on Bug/Steel). Scizor-Mega Bullet Punch (Technician+STAB, priority+1) is 2x SE on Mamoswine and Hatterene; Close Combat 2x SE on Meowscarada and Incineroar. Politoed Drizzle re-sets rain to enable 1-turn Electro Shot and weaken Fire moves. Noivern 192 Spe for speed control; Focus Sash preserved if switched to bench. Watch for Torkoal Protect (reduced success after 1 use) and opponent switching Torkoal to Mamoswine (Ground immune to Electric).

decisions.rationale: Archaludon at +3 SpA with LO is the primary win-condition threat and must be removed immediately. Mamoswine HHP (71.6-147.9%) + Metagross Meteor Mash (12.7-26.7%) combine for 84-175% damage, likely OHKOing. Speed order is uncertain (Mamo 132 vs Arch 105-137), but even if Archaludon moves first, removing it is worth risking Metagross at 9%. Scizor's Bullet Punch on Metagross is NVE, and Archaludon's Flash Cannon on Metagross is also NVE—Metagross may survive a hit anyway. Focusing both attacks ma
decisions.notebook: Archaludon Modest LO +3 SpA is the central threat; always prioritize removing it before it fires. Electro Shot charges in sun (no immediate damage), so Archaludon likely uses Flash Cannon or Earthquake instead. Mega Metagross at low HP is extremely fragile but Tough Claws Meteor Mash still provides meaningful chip on NVE Steel targets. Mamoswine Thickfat + Ice/Ground typing gives key resistances; Life Orb HHP is the primary Archaludon removal tool. Incineroar Focus Sash only triggers at full HP—preserve for late-game Intimidate cycles. Sun vs Rain weather war: Torkoal Drought overrides Politoed Drizzle when switched in. Opponent tends to Protect after taking heavy damage—predict accordingly. Noivern Timid Focus Sash outspeeds Mega Metagross; keep Ice Shard priority ready.

decisions.rationale: Double into Mamoswine: Flash Cannon 66-156% + Bullet Punch 30-66% combined guarantees KO before Mamoswine can High Horsepower. Metagross at 8% is harmless (all moves NVE 0.5x on Bug/Steel). Mega Evolve Scizor now for free—priority move means no speed cost this turn, gains bulk and Atk for cleanup of 8% Metagross + 13% Incineroar next.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Metagross+Incineroar; Metagross Protects turn 1, Meteor Mash turn 2, Protect turn 3, Protect turn 6 (3 total uses—Protect heavily penalized). Incineroar: Fake Out T1, Protect T2, Flare Blitz T3, Protect T4. Torkoal switched in T4 (Drought sun), fainted T6 to Electro Shot. Mamoswine brought in T6 as Torkoal replacement. Opponent tends to Protect Metagross to stall. Archaludon +3 SpA from 3 Electro Shot charges in sun (2-turn). Scizor-Mega base 150 Atk / 140 Def / 100 SpD / 75 Spe—Mega Evolve ASAP for bulk and speed; walls Metagross-Mega completely. Politoed burned, Sitrus consumed, low HP—bench for now. Noivern Focus Sash intact on bench. Sun has 2 turns left; if Politoed returns, Drizzle overrides sun for 1-turn Electro Shot. Game 1 near-closed: foe has Metagross 8% + Incineroar 13% remaining after Mamoswine KO.

decisions.rationale: Politoed's Drizzle makes Weather Ball 225 effective power (STAB+rain) — guaranteed KO on any remaining foe at single-digit HP. Scizor Bullet Punch (priority+1, 2x SE) KOs Mamoswine at 2%. Together they sweep both active foes this turn or next. Noivern's Hurricane is 50% accuracy in sun and can't guarantee KOs; preserve its Focus Sash for games 2-3.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Metagross+Incineroar; Metagross Protect-stalls heavily (3 Protect uses by T7). Incineroar: Fake Out T1, Protect T2, Flare Blitz T3, Protect T4. Torkoal brought T4, fainted T6. Mamoswine brought T6. Opponent tends to Protect Metagross to stall and preserve it. Metagross-Mega Jolly 143-178 Spe. Mamoswine Adamant 100-132 Spe ThickFat LifeOrb. Meowscarada (not brought G1): Jolly 157-192 Spe Protean ExpertBelt. Hatterene (not brought G1): Quiet 44-72 Spe MagicBounce Leftovers. For G2/G3: opponent likely leads Metagross+Incineroar again; consider Noivern Tailwind + Scizor-Mega as anti-lead. Politoed Drizzle+Weather Ball is premier cleanup tool. Archaludon Electro Shot in sun is 2-turn but +1 SpA per charge; in rain (Drizzle) it's 1-turn.

decisions.rationale: Mamoswine at 3% dies to any hit from Scizor or Politoed. HHP is 2x super effective on Scizor-Mega (Ground vs Steel), maximizing value before Mamoswine faints. Metagross Protects to survive Scizor's Close Combat and Politoed's attacks, preserving our last healthy-ish Pokémon. Metagross's attacks are all NVE vs Scizor, so attacking is inferior to Protecting. This line trades Mamoswine for meaningful Scizor damage while keeping Metagross alive to handle Noivern or Politoed next turn.
decisions.notebook: Archaludon Modest LO eliminated; Stamina boost irrelevant now. Scizor-Mega Adamant is primary physical threat with CC/BP; Ice Punch NVE vs Bug/Steel. Politoed burned Drizzle enables Water Weather Ball; Sitrus consumed. Noivern Timid FS Infiltrator is clean win condition if it sets Tailwind—must preserve priority (Ice Shard/BP) and consider Incineroar Intimidate cycles. Mamoswine Thickfat provides Fire/Ice resistances but 4x weak to Fighting. Metagross-Mega Tough Claws Meteor Mash reliable chip even NVE. Opponent Protects after heavy damage—predict on turns following big hits. Incineroar FS only useful at full HP; preserve for late-game. Rain vs Sun weather war favors opponent currently; Torkoal fainted.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Politoed Weather Ball (100 BP Water in rain, 2x SE vs Steel) guaranteed KOs Metagross at 8%. Even if one Protects, the other dies and it's 2v1 cleanup. Double Protect only stalls one turn — repeat next turn.

Protect preserves the Mega for late-game, avoids giving opponent a free KO, and scouts their play. Incineroar is fainted so must Pass. Rain favors opponent's Water attacks; preserving Metagross is critical vs Noivern Tailwind threat.

Bringing Torkoal (Drought) alongside Metagross-Mega left the team with zero Water resistance and no speed control to disrupt Politoed’s Drizzle. Once Rain locked, Politoed’s Weather Ball became super-effective and overwhelming, forcing Metagross-Mega into repeated Protect cycles until it fell to Scizor-Mega’s Close Combat. The four brought and intended Mega lacked the defensive synergy and offensive pressure needed to
reflections.adjustment: Replace Torkoal with a Grass-type or Water-immune pivot (e.g., Rillaboom or Amoonguss) to absorb Weather Ball, apply terrain/spore pressure, and provide speed control. Keep Metagross-Mega but pair it with a faster lead that can threaten Politoed before weather sets, and adjust the preview to prioritize a Water-resistant core that can safely cycle Intimidate and preserve priority for Noivern.
